name: parabolic_trough_receiver_forristal
title: Parabolic-trough receiver (HCE): steady 1D radial energy balance, Forristal/NREL model
summary: First-principles 1D radial energy balance of a parabolic-trough heat collector element (glass envelope, evacuated annulus with residual gas, forced convection to the wind, radiation to the sky), solved in steady state for a receiver at a given heat-transfer-fluid temperature; gives the heat loss per reflector area, the thermal and total efficiency and the temperatures of the tube and of the glass envelope.
language_features: temperature in K for the radiation terms

origin.course: scientific model of R. Forristall, NREL/TP-550-34169 (October 2003)

verification.reference: independent Python re-evaluation of the same equations (scipy fsolve, written from the Modelica source, script and CSV kept in the conversion work folder and deleted afterwards); physics cross-check against the measured heat losses and glass temperatures of the NREL PTR70 heat-loss test (F. Burkholder and C. Kutscher, NREL/TP-550-45633, May 2009, Table 3 and Table 4); energy-balance closure
verification.notes: 27 common variables, 0 differ at rtol = 1e-3 (maximum 2.35e-09 on err_bal). The glass mid temperature T_g is the one variable the source does not define consistently (its two definitions of Phi_glass_ext carry opposite signs); the CoolSolve solution is the physically ordered one, T_int_g > T_g > T_ext_g, and matches the reference re-evaluated in that form. The model reproduces the measured glass surface temperatures of the NREL test stand (35.0 and 80.1 degC) but over-predicts its heat-loss values by a factor 1.9 to 3.2; see README.

history.action: added (translation of ThermoCycle SolAbsForristal, card C-89)
